chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Raja', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Good neighbourliness increases in the sustenance.

key_terms.حُسْنُ الْجِوَارِ: Good neighbourliness / Excellence in neighbourly relations

ai.seo_question: How does good neighbourliness affect one's sustenance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the ethical practice of 'husn al-jawar' (good neighborliness) directly to increased rizq, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social rights (huquq al-nas) as a means of spiritual and material blessing. This narration underscores that neighborly conduct is not merely social etiquette but a divine mechanism for sustaining livelihood, a concept deeply rooted in the broader Islamic tradition of community cohesion.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ismail Bin Mihran, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Raja’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Isma’il ibn Mehran from Ibrahim ibn abu Raja’ from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Maintaining good neighborly relations increases one’s sustenance.”
